analysis.title: Weekly Wrap: Is the Semis Sell-Off Over?
key_insights: HF net flows in US Semis were below -3z for the second week in a row. HF selling extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record, with unusually large cumulative net selling.
Flows varied by region: Japan also saw selling, AxJ was roughly balanced and EMEA Semis were bought. Retail flows suggested dip-buying and Tech ETFs saw inflows.

Global HF net exposure to Semis has fallen 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025. The global long/short ratio declined from 4.4x to 2.1x. Retail sentiment toward Semis is at a very low level.
With the combined 6m positioning + price z-score near -3z, JPM sees a possible bounce similar to the one that followed the same type of reduction in Momentum by late July.

Global Semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile versus data since 2018, so positioning is not especially low on a long-term basis. The 6m z-score of HF positioning is below the 6m z-score of relative returns, so history suggests a rebound may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish.

Gross flows and HF performance showed signs of stabilization. After near -2z de-grossing on Monday, flows calmed Tuesday to Thursday, and Thursday was the most positive global re-gross day in about a month. Multi-Strat gross flows also rebounded from recent extremes.
HF performance gained about 1.5% over five days and is roughly flat month to date globally (-0.3% across All Strategies). Europe is up 1.7% MTD and Asia is down 2%.
HF gross leverage fell 4% week over week while net leverage was broadly unchanged. The US Tactical Positioning Monitor was little changed at the 20th percentile since 2015.

Europe rebounded faster from depressed positioning alongside outperformance. European flows are up +1.5z relative to US flows over the past 1-3 months, which brings relative EU positioning (vs. US) back to neutral.

Japan was broadly sold. HF flows were -1.4z WoW and -2.3z MoM, with nearly all sectors sold during the week and all 11 sectors sold over the month. Combined Japan positioning (HFs, CTAs, margin balances) fell to the 24th percentile since 2015, near year-to-date lows.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning has reset sharply and sentiment is depressed, so a near-term rebound is possible. A durable rebound likely needs renewed HF buying, and long-term positioning is still around the 80th percentile.

risk_factors: HF de-risking in Semis may continue early in the week.
